tortured_phrases_cases.text: In this work we propose a novel approach using profound learning techniques to classify medical images. The profound learning architecture achieves state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets.
tortured_phrases_cases.note: Classic paper-mill substitution. 'Profound' replaces 'deep' throughout. Detected via Cabanac & Labbé 2021 tortured-phrase lexicon.

tortured_phrases_cases.text: The proposed methodology employs a profound chain of connections with ten concealed layers to extract hierarchical feature representations from raw input signals.
tortured_phrases_cases.note: Multi-word substitution for 'deep neural network'. Particularly diagnostic when combined with 'concealed layers' (tortured 'hidden layers').

tortured_phrases_cases.text: To evaluate the robustness of our framework, we also trained a sham system with randomized weights to establish a performance lower bound for comparison.
tortured_phrases_cases.note: Sham substituted for dummy. Common in paper-mill outputs from Chinese paper mills detected in 2021 Scopus/WoS audit.

tortured_phrases_cases.text: The quantity movement of financial returns was examined using ARIMA models on daily closing prices from 2015 through 2022.
tortured_phrases_cases.note: Substitution of 'quantitative' with 'quantity movement' — statistically improbable in authentic academic writing.

tortured_phrases_cases.text: The experimental results showed irregular and wonderful outcomes under extreme stress conditions, with variance exceeding three standard deviations from baseline.
tortured_phrases_cases.note: Subtle transformation: 'remarkable' → 'wonderful'. Phrase appears in multiple paper-mill outputs in materials science journals.

tortured_phrases_cases.text: The characteristic building framework was designed to automatically learn discriminative features from raw pixel values without handcrafted feature engineering.
tortured_phrases_cases.note: Feature extraction architecture tortured into 'characteristic building framework'. Identified in paper-mill outputs targeting computer vision venues.

tortured_phrases_cases.text: The system performs irregular region highlight by comparing pixel intensity distributions against a Gaussian background model updated online.
tortured_phrases_cases.note: 'Anomaly detection' → 'irregular region highlight'. Cabanac & Labbé listed this as high-confidence paper-mill indicator.

tortured_phrases_cases.text: The property extrication module processes raw sensor readings and outputs a 256-dimensional embedding vector fed into the classification head.
tortured_phrases_cases.note: 'Feature extraction' → 'property extrication'. One of the most frequently identified phrases in Cabanac & Labbé 2021 dataset.

tortured_phrases_cases.text: Hormonal regulation of breast milk emission is controlled by prolactin secreted from the anterior pituitary in response to suckling stimulation.
tortured_phrases_cases.note: 'Lactation' → 'breast milk emission'. Appeared in SCIgen-adjacent paper-mill outputs in biomedical journals. Highly diagnostic.

tortured_phrases_cases.text: Our model outperforms counterfeit neural systems on the MNIST benchmark, achieving 99.2% accuracy with only 50K training examples.
tortured_phrases_cases.note: 'Artificial neural networks' → 'counterfeit neural systems'. Artificial → counterfeit substitution is a known paper-mill pattern.

tortured_phrases_cases.text: This enormous amount work builds on prior studies to demonstrate scalable processing of high-dimensional biomedical datasets using distributed computing frameworks.
tortured_phrases_cases.note: 'Large-scale' → 'enormous amount work'. Grammatically anomalous; high precision signal for automated detection.

tortured_phrases_cases.text: Handling massive amounts of knowledge remains a central challenge in modern information retrieval systems, particularly in low-latency environments.
tortured_phrases_cases.note: 'Big data' → 'massive amounts of knowledge'. Paraphrase evasion pattern common in paper-mill submissions.

tortured_phrases_cases.text: In recent years, deep learning has emerged as the dominant paradigm for computer vision tasks, outperforming traditional hand-crafted feature methods on large-scale benchmarks such as ImageNet.
tortured_phrases_cases.note: Legitimate academic prose using standard terminology. No tortured phrases present.

tortured_phrases_cases.text: Anomaly detection methods based on deep neural networks have shown promising results in industrial fault diagnosis, particularly when labeled anomaly data is scarce.
tortured_phrases_cases.note: Clean academic text using correct domain terminology. Negative control.

grim_test_cases.grim_check: 25 × 3.53 = 88.25 — not an integer, therefore impossible for N=25 integer responses
grim_test_cases.note: Inspired by Wansink pizza lab papers. With N=25 and 1-7 Likert scale, mean must be k/25 for integer k. 88.25 is not an integer sum.

grim_test_cases.grim_check: 40 × 4.27 = 170.8 — not an integer, therefore impossible for N=40 integer responses
grim_test_cases.note: N=40 requires mean to be multiple of 0.025. 4.27 → 40×4.27=170.8. Not achievable with integer Likert responses.

grim_test_cases.grim_check: 30 × 2.71 = 81.3 — not an integer, therefore impossible for N=30 integer responses
grim_test_cases.note: With N=30, achievable means must satisfy 30k for some integer k. 2.71×30=81.3 — impossible. Resembles errors in Wansink et al. 2013.

grim_test_cases.grim_check: 28 × 5.49 = 153.72 — not an integer, therefore impossible for N=28 integer responses
grim_test_cases.note: Brown & Heathers (2017) report this class of error is surprisingly common in social psychology. N=28 requires mean to step in 1/28 ≈ 0.0357 increments.

grim_test_cases.grim_check: 15 × 3.17 = 47.55 — not an integer, therefore impossible for N=15 integer responses
grim_test_cases.note: Small sample (N=15) with reported mean of 3.17. 15×3.17=47.55 — non-integer, GRIM failure. Found in self-report questionnaire studies.

grim_test_cases.grim_check: 25 × 3.56 = 89.0 — integer, therefore this mean is achievable for N=25
grim_test_cases.note: Valid mean: 25×3.56=89 exactly. GRIM test passes. This is a plausible and mathematically consistent value.

grim_test_cases.grim_check: 20 × 4.20 = 84.0 — integer, therefore this mean is achievable for N=20
grim_test_cases.note: Valid mean: 20×4.20=84. GRIM passes. Negative control.

statcheck_cases.note: F(2,45)=3.21 yields p≈0.049, not p=.028. Discrepancy of ~0.021. The reported p-value is too small by roughly a factor of 2. Nuijten et al. 2016 categorised this type as gross inconsistency.
t(48)=2.15 yields two-tailed p≈0.037, not p=.015. Reported p is significantly smaller than the correct value. Classic statcheck error type found in ~50% of psychology articles per Nuijten et al.
χ²(3)=8.14 correctly yields p≈0.043. This is a correctly reported statistic. Negative control.

t(32)=1.89 two-tailed p≈0.068 (not significant at α=0.05). Reported p=.034 would make it significant — a direction-changing error. Nuijten et al. found ~1% of papers contain errors that change conclusions.
F(1,98)=7.84 correctly yields p≈0.006. Valid APA statistic. Negative control.
F(3,120)=4.52 yields p≈0.005. Reported p=.002 is significantly lower than correct value. Error suggests possible rounding or transcription mistake in manuscript.
Pearson r(58)=.41 with N=60 yields p≈0.001. Correctly reported. Negative control for correlation statistics.

l1_intent_cases.citing_sentence: Consistent with the findings of [Smith et al. 2021], our results confirm that sleep deprivation significantly impairs declarative memory consolidation in young adults.
l1_intent_cases.abstract_of_cited: We investigated the effects of 24-hour sleep deprivation on memory consolidation in 42 healthy adults. Results demonstrated significant impairment in declarative memory tasks (p < .001, d = 0.87) compared to rested controls, with no significant effect on procedural memory.
l1_intent_cases.note: Clear supporting citation — citing sentence accurately reflects the cited paper's finding about declarative memory impairment. No misrepresentation. Intent: SUPPORTING.

l1_intent_cases.citing_sentence: In contrast to [Jones et al. 2019] who found no significant effect, our experiment demonstrates a robust relationship between social media use and depression in adolescents.
l1_intent_cases.abstract_of_cited: A longitudinal study of 1,200 adolescents found no statistically significant association between time spent on social media platforms and depression symptom scores (r = .04, p = .31) after controlling for pre-existing mental health conditions.
l1_intent_cases.note: Clear contrasting citation — the citing paper accurately represents that Jones et al. found a null result and uses it as a contrast point. Intent: CONTRASTING.

l1_intent_cases.citing_sentence: Several studies have examined machine learning applications in clinical decision support [Johnson 2020; Kim 2021; Patel 2022].
l1_intent_cases.abstract_of_cited: We present a machine learning system for early sepsis detection in ICU patients, achieving AUROC of 0.91. The system integrates vital signs, lab results, and medication records to provide real-time risk scores.
l1_intent_cases.note: Background mentioning citation — paper is listed among a group of references for broad context, not specifically engaged. Intent: MENTIONING.

l1_intent_cases.citing_sentence: As demonstrated by [Williams et al. 2018], the intervention led to a 40% reduction in hospital readmissions, supporting the efficacy of our adapted protocol.
l1_intent_cases.abstract_of_cited: This pilot study of 28 patients tested a transitional care intervention for heart failure. While patient satisfaction improved (p = .04), readmission rates did not differ significantly from controls (18% vs. 22%, p = .61) over 90 days.
l1_intent_cases.note: MISREPRESENTATION: citing sentence claims 40% reduction in readmissions, but Williams 2018 found NO significant reduction. This is a fabricated or hallucinated quantitative claim attributed to the cited paper. Signal: citation_misrepresents_source.

l1_intent_cases.citing_sentence: Previous research [Brown 2019; Davis 2020; Lee 2021; Chen 2022; Park 2023] has investigated neural networks. Deep learning approaches [Kim 2019; Wang 2020; Zhang 2021] have been proposed. Various datasets [Liu 2020; Yang 2021] have been used.
l1_intent_cases.abstract_of_cited: Multiple cited papers cover different aspects of neural network research.
l1_intent_cases.note: ALL_CITATIONS_MENTIONING case: every citation in this passage is a superficial background reference with no substantive engagement. No paper is cited as supporting or contrasting any specific claim. This is a red flag for padding.

l1_intent_cases.citing_sentence: Following the methodology of [Thompson et al. 2020], we applied a transformer-based architecture pre-trained on PubMed abstracts and fine-tuned on our clinical corpus.
l1_intent_cases.abstract_of_cited: We introduce BioBERT, a pre-training procedure for biomedical text mining tasks. BioBERT is pre-trained on PubMed abstracts and PMC full-text articles and fine-tuned on downstream biomedical NLP tasks, achieving state-of-the-art performance.
l1_intent_cases.note: USING citation — correctly describes adopting the cited paper's methodology. No misrepresentation. Intent: USING.

l2_nli_cases.claim: The drug reduced mortality by 35% compared to placebo in the randomised controlled trial.
l2_nli_cases.source_text: In our double-blind RCT of 340 patients, the treatment group showed no statistically significant difference in 30-day mortality compared to placebo (15.2% vs. 16.8%, HR = 0.91, 95% CI 0.63-1.31, p = .61). The drug was well tolerated with a favourable safety profile.
l2_nli_cases.note: Clear contradiction: citing paper claims 35% mortality reduction but the source reports no significant difference (p=.61). The claim inverts the source's null result. LR=6.0 for claim_contradicted.

l2_nli_cases.claim: Exposure to social media for more than 3 hours per day was associated with significantly higher rates of depression among teenagers.
l2_nli_cases.source_text: We examined social media usage patterns in 856 adolescents aged 13-18 using ecological momentary assessment. Passive consumption (scrolling without interacting) showed a moderate positive correlation with depressive symptoms (r = 0.34, p < .001). Active social interaction online was not significantly associated with depression.
l2_nli_cases.note: The source shows a correlation for passive use but does not specifically address '3 hours' threshold or overall depression rates. Claim is partially but not fully supported. No outright contradiction. Negative for claim_contradicted.

l2_nli_cases.claim: The neural network achieved 98.5% accuracy on the ImageNet benchmark.
l2_nli_cases.source_text: We evaluate our ResNet-50 baseline on CIFAR-10 and Fashion-MNIST benchmarks, achieving 94.3% and 93.1% accuracy respectively. We did not evaluate on ImageNet due to computational constraints.
l2_nli_cases.note: The source explicitly did not evaluate on ImageNet. The claim attributes an ImageNet result to a paper that never reported one. Signal: claim_unsupported with high confidence.

l2_nli_cases.claim: Patients who received the intervention showed significant improvements in quality of life compared to controls.
l2_nli_cases.source_text: A 12-week randomised trial assessed quality of life using the SF-36 questionnaire in 180 patients. The intervention group showed statistically significant improvements across all eight SF-36 domains compared to wait-list controls (all p < .05, effect sizes ranging from d = 0.41 to d = 0.76).
l2_nli_cases.note: The claim accurately reflects the source. The source directly supports the assertion of significant quality of life improvement. Negative control — signal should NOT fire.

l2_nli_cases.claim: Climate change will cause a 4°C rise in global temperatures by 2050 according to the IPCC.
l2_nli_cases.source_text: Under the SSP5-8.5 high-emissions scenario, global mean surface temperature is projected to increase by 3.3-5.7°C above pre-industrial levels by 2100. By 2050, warming of 1.5-2.0°C is expected under most scenarios. The IPCC sixth assessment report emphasizes that limiting warming to 1.5°C requires immediate and deep emissions reductions.
l2_nli_cases.note: The source (IPCC AR6) projects 4°C by 2100 in worst case, not 2050. The claim misattributes the timeframe by 50 years. Clear factual misrepresentation of the source. LR=6.0.

l2_nli_cases.claim: The study found that mindfulness meditation reduced cortisol levels by 23% after 8 weeks of practice.
l2_nli_cases.source_text: We conducted an 8-week MBSR (Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction) program with 64 adults. Salivary cortisol measurements at morning, noon, and evening were taken at baseline and post-intervention. A significant reduction in morning cortisol was observed (23.4% reduction, p = .002, Cohen's d = 0.68), with smaller non-significant reductions at other timepoints.
l2_nli_cases.note: The claim accurately reports the 23% cortisol reduction finding from the source. Well-supported citation. Negative control.

l2_nli_cases.claim: The antibiotic was found to be effective against gram-positive bacteria with a minimum inhibitory concentration below 0.5 μg/mL.
l2_nli_cases.source_text: In vitro susceptibility testing of compound X against 24 clinical isolates of gram-negative Enterobacteriaceae demonstrated MIC90 values of 0.25 μg/mL. Testing against Staphylococcus aureus (gram-positive) showed MIC90 values of 64 μg/mL, indicating poor activity against gram-positive organisms.
l2_nli_cases.note: The claim states effectiveness against gram-positive bacteria with low MIC, but the source explicitly shows poor activity (MIC=64 μg/mL) against gram-positive S. aureus. The claim reverses the finding direction.

l2_nli_cases.claim: Previous work has explored the use of transformer architectures for protein structure prediction.
l2_nli_cases.source_text: We introduce a transformer-based architecture that models protein sequence-structure relationships. Our model, trained on PDB structures, achieves competitive performance on CASP14 benchmarks and demonstrates that attention mechanisms can capture long-range residue interactions relevant to tertiary structure.
l2_nli_cases.note: Weak MENTIONING claim that is fully supported by the source content. The source is about transformer architectures for protein structure. Negative control.
